name: Gout
definition: Inflammatory arthritis caused by monosodium urate crystal deposition, presenting with acute flares, intercritical disease and sometimes tophi or chronic arthropathy.

typical: Abrupt severe joint pain, swelling, warmth and erythema
First MTP is common but any joint may be affected
Tophi may occur in chronic disease

redFlags.item: Septic arthritis must be excluded in an acutely hot swollen joint, especially with fever or immunosuppression
Gout and joint infection can coexist

core: Renal, cardiovascular and metabolic comorbidity assessment

investigations.principle: Synovial-fluid crystal identification is the diagnostic standard when feasible and uncertainty exists.
investigations.MRI: MRI is not routine for typical gout.
investigations.radiographs: Ultrasound or dual-energy CT may support selected difficult diagnoses; radiographs show chronic erosive change.

green: Treat acute flares promptly using an appropriate anti-inflammatory strategy
Address weight, alcohol and dietary factors as adjuncts
amber: NSAID, colchicine, corticosteroid and urate-lowering choices require renal, hepatic, cardiovascular, interaction and comorbidity review.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Vatarakta may be a useful Ayurvedic clinical correlation in selected presentations; crystal disease remains the modern diagnosis.

patientEducation.summary: Inflammatory arthritis caused by monosodium urate crystal deposition, presenting with acute flares, intercritical disease and sometimes tophi or chronic arthropathy.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for new/progressive major weakness, gait deterioration, bladder/bowel dysfunction, saddle sensory loss, fever/systemic illness with severe spinal/joint pain, major trauma, or other listed red flags.

sources.title: 2020 Guideline for the Management of Gout
